absent: Locking, concurrency and interrupt-mask rules around shared info, multicall batching and PMU updates are not shown.
Hypercall entry mechanics, register assignment and error-code meanings beyond return status are not shown.
Writers and lifecycle for physical-to-machine tables, GDT and LDT setup and trap-table installation are not shown.
Real grant-table foreign-mapping logic, page allocation and teardown paths are not shown; only a stub reporting success appears.

findings.text: Provides a multicall slot initializer for stack switching. It tags the entry with the stack-switch operation identifier, stores the supplied stack segment and stack pointer into the first two argument positions, and records a trace event noting two arguments.

Exposes scheduling and timing control. One helper forwards a scheduler command plus opaque argument and returns host status. A second splits a 64-bit deadline into low and high halves for the timer call. A third requests suspend by issuing a scheduler shutdown with suspend reason, placing the start-info frame number in the third hypercall word for tooling.

Exposes machine and platform services. Machine-check and platform operations stamp their request structures with the expected interface version before invoking a single-argument call. Version query, physical CPU telemetry and hardware virtualization helpers forward opcode plus argument and return host status.

Exposes memory, communication and device services as thin wrappers around two- or three-word calls: memory operations, batched multicalls, event-channel control, console output with command count and buffer, physical-device control, grant-table batching with count, virtual-machine assist toggles, per-CPU control, and device-model operations. The device-model path briefly permits supervisor access to user mappings around the call.

Provides guest-side Xen detection and a trivial MSI hook. Detection compares the hypervisor CPUID brand against the fixed Xen signature and derives a base leaf for further leaves. The initial-domain MSI restore helper unconditionally reports success.

Defines an abstraction for guest pointers shared with the host. Depending on build mode the handle is either a struct wrapping a native pointer or a bare native pointer, with helpers to define handles for named types and struct types. Setter helpers assign the supplied address and, in wide-handle configurations, first clear the whole slot to avoid leaking upper bits.

Trap table entry carries an exception vector, a flags byte, a code selector and a code offset. Flags encode privilege level in low bits and an event-mask control in a higher bit, with small accessors to read privilege and mask state and to set them.

Architecture portion of shared info tracks the physical-to-machine table. It holds a maximum frame count, a frame-list root with sentinel values for unset and invalid states, an NMI reason, and an optional linear mapping described by address-space root, virtual base and generation counter. The generation counter is bumped before and after updates so external readers can detect torn reads, with odd values meaning update in progress and element stores required to be atomic.

Virtual CPU construction context starts with an aligned floating-point area, followed by flag word, user register image, full 256-entry virtual trap table, LDT base and count, GDT frame list and count, kernel stack selector and pointer, control and debug register arrays, callback entry points, VM-assist bitmap and, on 64-bit, segment bases. Flags record floating-point validity, kernel context, event-disable behavior for failsafe and syscall paths, and online state.

32-bit user register image preserves general registers, private error and vector fields, instruction pointer, selector and flag state with a saved event-mask byte tied to interrupt flag, stack pointer and segment selectors. Companion per-CPU info holds fault address plus padding to fixed size, callback pairs hold selector and address, and timestamps use 64-bit cycle counters.

64-bit user register image preserves extended registers with dual-width accessors for legacy subregisters, private error and vector fields, instruction pointer, selector, saved event-mask with padding, flags tied to mask state, stack pointer and selectors where nonzero FS and GS override base addresses. Interrupt-return context orders result, flags and frame fields from stack top. Per-CPU and callback state collapse to compact forms.

Performance-monitoring structures separate architecture-neutral and vendor parts. AMD context stores positions of counter and control banks followed by a flexible register array. Intel context adds global control, overflow, status, fixed-control, debug-store, sampling-enable and debug-control fields plus fixed and architectural positions and a flexible array. Counter pairs hold counter and control values, sampled register snapshots hold instruction pointer, stack, flags, selectors and privilege, and the top container unions register snapshot, flags, virtualized LAPIC entry and vendor context with reserved padding for growth.

Virtual layout: up to 32 virtual CPUs; GDT reservation starts at page 14 with byte and entry derivations; 32-bit hypervisor and machine windows start at 0xF5800000 with machine window ending at 0xF6800000 and shift 2; 64-bit hypervisor window spans 0xFFFF800000000000 to 0xFFFF880000000000 and machine window to 0xFFFF804000000000 with shift 3; entry count derives from window span shifted; trap uses vector 0x82; CPUID can be prefixed for emulation; frame and long types are native width with hex print forms.

Segment and conversion ABI: 32-bit flat selectors use 0xe019 for ring1 code, 0xe021 for ring1 data and stack, 0xe02b for ring3 code and 0xe033 for ring3 data and stack with kernel and user aliases; 64-bit uses 0xe023 and 0xe033 for code, 0xe02b for data and stack and 0x0000 for 64-bit kernel and user data with width-specific aliases; segment-base indices are 0 to 3 for FS, user GS, kernel GS and selector-carried GS; 32-bit frame conversion folds with 12-bit shift and 20-bit wrap while 64-bit shifts by 12; PMU flags occupy bits 0 to 3 for cached, user, real-mode and paravirtual; in-syscall flag is bit 8; Xen brand is XenVMMXenVMM.
Machine and physical addresses are wrapped in distinct single-field structs with constructors from raw values, keeping the two address spaces type-separated in the interface.

Physical address limit is either a 52-bit SME-cleared range or the generic physical mask depending on configuration, and page-table machine-frame mask combines page mask with that limit. Invalid table entries use all-ones, top two bits tag foreign and identity frames with helpers to apply them, and entries per page derives from page size over word size.

Guest entry points for events, failsafe and system calls are carried as addresses in the virtual CPU context, with 32-bit form pairing selector and address and 64-bit form using address alone. Construction macros build these entries from supplied code location.

Risk points: device-model calls must bracket host access with user-access guards or risk faults; suspend must place the start-info frame in the third word or tooling loses resume state; linear table readers must retry on odd generation or changed counts; PMU register banks are partly read-only to guests and updates are validated on flush with only the mask bit of the virtualized LAPIC entry honored; foreign and identity frame tags must be masked before use as real frames; wide guest-handle stores must clear upper bits.
Each header is protected by a unique include guard macro preventing multiple inclusion within a translation unit.
Foreign mapping helper for grant-table operations is a no-op stub in this configuration, accepting map operation arrays, page list and count and reporting success without altering state.

Linear table publication follows stable, updating, stable. Writers advance the generation counter to an odd value, modify entries with atomic stores, then advance again to even. Readers sample the counter, read entries, then re-sample and retry if the counter changed or was odd at either sample.
